text:
Luke Hughes has six goals in 19 games, already level with his total from all of last season, and he's playing more than 24 minutes a night. He also traded punches with Matthew Schaefer in a heated Islanders game, which is not a sentence anyone expected to write about him.

The goals will slow. He's shooting 14% against 4% last season on 3.3 expected goals. But the more important change is at five on five, where New Jersey takes 56% of the expected goals with him on. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him giving up more chances than almost any defenseman (bottom 3%), and The Hockey News has been writing about him leaning into his strengths this year.

He gets to dangerous ice for a defenseman (87th percentile in chances from the slot, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking). At 23, the question is whether the defensive improvement holds once the shooting cools. Our range: 36 to 57 points.
